activities.anchor: what technology permits versus what culture wants to say
activities.caption: pair each structural kit with the style it built
activities.name: hsKitMatch

config.prompt: Every style is a kit before it is a look — match kit to style:

pairs.left: pointed arch + ribbed vault + flying buttress
pairs.right: Gothic — the stone skeleton with glass infill
the Crystal Palace — production outrunning theory
the Chicago skyscraper — the load-bearing wall dies

config.why: The kit changes with materials; the theory changes more slowly — and the conversation between them is the engine of the whole story.

activities.anchor: revivable at will
activities.caption: fill the blanks — Greek optics and Roman records
activities.name: hsClassicalCloze

config.text: The Parthenon refines proportion with optical corrections — columns swell (%%0%%) and lean inward because perfect straightness looks wrong. Rome's Pantheon dome, at %%1%% metres, is still the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome.
config.hint: One is the name of the swelling; the other is the Pantheon's record, held for nearly two millennia.

activities.anchor: architectural history grades them separately
activities.caption: bet first — older arches, Roman fame
activities.name: hsArchPredict

config.q: Arched drains and gates existed in Mesopotamia and Egypt millennia before Rome. Why, then, do we credit Rome?
choices: Rome industrialised the arch — vaults, domes, aqueduct bridges — and paired it with pozzolana concrete
Roman arches used a secret stone formula since lost
The older arches were only decorative, never structural
config.why: Invention and deployment are different chapters: Rome multiplied the arch into a system for making space at scale — and history grades them separately.

activities.anchor: in a real sense, their descendant
activities.caption: rebuild the Gothic redirection — from fortress to skeleton
activities.name: hsGothicOrder

config.prompt: Put the Gothic kit's moves in order:
items: Romanesque barrel vaults push outward along their whole length — walls must be massive
Pointed arches steepen the thrust toward the vertical
Ribbed vaults concentrate the load onto ribs and piers instead of whole walls
Flying buttresses catch the outward thrust outside the wall and deliver it to the ground
Walls dissolve into stained glass — the structural surplus spent on theology
config.why: The Gothic kit redirected forces instead of merely resisting them — Amiens' 42.3 m nave and Beauvais' 48.5 m (whose choir fell in 1284, the era's honest statement of its factor of safety).

activities.anchor: the facade becomes a curtain, hung
activities.caption: file the rupture's innovations — what problem did each solve?
activities.name: hsRuptureBuckets

config.prompt: The 19th century broke structure = masonry three ways. File each innovation:

items.label: steel frames carrying the loads (Home Insurance Building, 1885)
Paxton's standardised kit of cast-iron parts
the facade demoted to a hung curtain
a 564 m exhibition hall assembled in months

config.why: Structure decoupled from walls, height made usable, and production outrunning theory — the rupture ran on three threads at once.

activities.anchor: a description of surface, not of temperament
activities.caption: call the magnitude — Beauvais' honest limit
activities.name: hsBeauvaisEstimate

config.prompt: Amiens' nave reaches 42.3 m and Beauvais' choir 48.5 m — until the vaults fell in 1284. Roughly how many metres taller was Beauvais than Amiens?
config.why: 48.5 − 42.3 ≈ 6.2 m — the vertical race's last bid, and the collapse that stated the factor of safety honestly.
config.context: Gothic was high technology: the structural systems lesson of this atlas is its descendant.

activities.anchor: the future keeps borrowing from what the canon forgot
activities.caption: true or false — beyond the canon
activities.name: hsCanonJudge

statements.s: A Yazdi badgir is a stack-effect cooling machine; a thick adobe wall is a thermal flywheel lagging temperatures about 8–10 hours.
statements.why: Vernacular architecture is passive-design R&D performed over centuries by trial.

statements.s: East Asian timber pagodas survive earthquakes because their joints are rigid.
statements.why: The bracket-set joints FLEX — Hōryū-ji has stood since the 7th century because the frame moves.

statements.s: Djenné's Great Mosque is the world's largest mud building, replastered annually as a civic festival.
statements.why: Malian vernacular — maintenance as festival, engineering as culture.

statements.s: Vernacular buildings are folk art with no technical content.
statements.why: Courtyards are night-sky radiators; wind-catchers are cooling machines — validated by modern heat-transfer analysis.

activities.anchor: rather than merely memorising
activities.caption: bet first — why the frame wore Gothic clothes
activities.name: hsStylePredict

config.q: The steel frame arrived in 1885 — yet American clients spent fifty more years wrapping it in Gothic and classical clothing. Why?
choices: Because cultures choose: banks and courthouses wanted to speak permanence
Exposed steel was too expensive until the 1930s
config.why: Materials permit; cultures choose. Technology writes the possible; the style debate writes the actual — which is why the history is argued, not memorised.

activities.anchor: it is a wish, not a design
activities.caption: pair each drawing with what it exists to show
activities.name: psSetMatch

config.prompt: The drawing set is a language — match each part to its job:

pairs.left: the plan — a horizontal cut about 1.2 m above the floor
pairs.right: walls, door leaves, window openings — the choreography in ink

pairs.left: the section — a vertical cut, near half removed
pairs.right: heights and structure — the vertical argument

pairs.left: the elevation — a view without a cut

pairs.right: the window head, the roof edge — where water is defeated

config.why: Until a thing has a dimension, a level and a junction, it is a wish, not a design — deciding is drawing.

activities.anchor: that ambiguity is now a drawn, checkable fact
activities.caption: bet first — Monge's classified geometry
activities.name: psMongePredict

config.q: Why did the French military classify Gaspard Monge's descriptive geometry as a state secret in the 1780s–90s?
choices: Because it let fortifications be designed and fabricated from paper alone
Because it decrypted the royal correspondence
Because the drawings could be forged with it
config.why: Truth from paper: every length true in its plane or derivable from two drawings — a military capability before it was a classroom subject.

activities.anchor: reviewers read plans knowing which claims
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the workhorse scale and the comfort rule
activities.name: psScaleCloze

config.text: At 1:100 — the general-arrangement workhorse — a 900 mm door becomes %%0%% mm of line. At 1:50, the staircase comfort rule reads two risers plus one tread ≈ %%1%% mm.
config.hint: The scale divides by 100; the comfort rule is the arithmetic every stair must satisfy.

activities.anchor: Graphic convention here is not decoration; it is compression
activities.caption: rebuild the plan-reading sequence
activities.name: psReadOrder

config.prompt: A plan is a social script. Put the reading in order:
items: Start where the building does: the entrance
Trace the arrival choreography — compression, then release
Follow the unavoidable circulation: corridors, stairs, lifts
Check the adjacencies — kitchen to dining, bedroom to bathroom, clean vs dirty routes
Read the light: orientations, and the depth of the plan's darkest corners
config.why: The daylight rule of thumb: roughly 2–2.5× window-head-height is as deep as useful daylight reaches — service spaces beyond, or someone's desk.

activities.anchor: a model, not a design
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the dimension string
activities.name: psStringSpot

config.prompt: One line of this dimensioning answer is wrong — click it:
lines: A dimension string runs: 2100 + 1800 + 1500 against an overall of 5390.
The segments sum to 5400, leaving a 10 mm rounding residue.
Adjust one segment so the sum closes exactly at 5390.
Or leave the string open — the crew will absorb the 10 mm at the most visible corner.
config.correction: Close the string — push any discrepancy into a designed joint, where it belongs.
config.why: A string that does not close forces the crew to improvise the residue somewhere, usually at the worst place. Closing it makes the tolerance a designed act.

activities.anchor: humans conceive and decide
activities.caption: bet first — what clash detection actually catches
activities.name: psClashPredict

config.q: BIM's clash detection runs overnight on the model. What does it actually catch?
choices: Every duct intersecting every beam and every pipe with every soffit — on Tuesday instead of on site, with a hammer and a change order
config.why: The immediate dividend is geometric: the software intersects everything with everything. The deeper dividend is coordination — how a modern hospital, miles of services through a structural grid, is even possible.

activities.anchor: Professionals read sets, never sheets
activities.caption: true or false — the language's fine print
activities.name: psSetJudge

statements.s: A plan without its section is wrong about heights.
statements.why: Drawings are a communication protocol — lossless only if the whole set is read together.

statements.s: The specification outranks the drawings where they conflict.
statements.why: The written book of materials and workmanship is the arbiter.

statements.s: Any scale will do to start — you can always zoom in later.
statements.why: Scale is a commitment level, not magnification: a casual line at 1:200 is a stack of physical layers at 1:5.

statements.s: A detail that is beautiful and unbuildable is a model, not a design.
statements.why: Every junction must be buildable by a real crew, in the drawn sequence, in the rain, with the crane they have.

activities.anchor: it is the non-negotiable leg
activities.caption: file the fire defences — passive or active?
activities.name: wbFireBuckets

config.prompt: Most of fire safety is invisible. File each defence:

items.label: compartmentation — keeping fire in one zone
protected stairs sized by calculable escape times

config.why: The active systems buy minutes; the passive design buys the hours — and it is the layer the Grenfell inquiry found had drifted from substance into appearance.

activities.anchor: drifted from substance into appearance
activities.caption: bet first — why the steel tower still stands
activities.name: wbSteelPredict

config.q: Steel loses half its strength around 550–600 °C. Why does a fireproofed steel tower still stand long enough to evacuate?
choices: Because coatings and boards delay the steel from reaching those temperatures
Because steel actually gains strength when hot
Because building fires never reach 550 °C indoors
config.why: The strength collapse is real — which is why material behaviour is a design input, not a footnote, and why the passive layer is where the hours are bought.

activities.anchor: with exam scores attached
activities.caption: fill the blanks — fabric first, then the numbers
activities.name: wbFabricCloze

config.text: Fabric first: orient, insulate, %%0%% and shade — and the Passivhaus space-heating target sits under %%1%% kWh/m²·year, roughly a tenth of conventional. Neglect ventilation and an occupied room drifts past %%2%% ppm of CO₂ within an hour.
config.hint: Four passive moves, one demanding target, and the CO₂ number that slows decision-making.

activities.anchor: a health intervention wearing a planning vocabulary
activities.caption: pair the study with what it found
activities.name: wbHealthMatch

config.prompt: The measurable shadows of design — match study to finding:

pairs.right: tree-facing surgery patients needed fewer analgesics, discharged sooner
mapped cholera deaths around the Broad Street pump — epidemiology founded
public health's greatest infrastructure, built in brick
associated with hypertension and learning deficits

config.why: The built environment acts on bodies in ways that are now measured — which is why school siting treats traffic as a clinical variable.

activities.anchor: rather than worshipping one
activities.caption: bet first — why brutalist estates failed
activities.name: wbVenusPredict

config.q: Brutalist estates that failed socially most often failed where…
choices: their public spaces felt illegible or unsafe — Newman's defensible-space work tied layout legibility to vandalism rates
the raw concrete was structurally too strong
residents disliked the colour of the facade
config.why: Venustas is load-bearing: people maintain, respect and revisit buildings they find beautiful — and longevity is the greenest quality a building can have.

activities.anchor: retrofits carry more climate leverage than most showpieces
activities.caption: call the magnitude — cement's share
activities.name: wbCementEstimate

config.prompt: Roughly what per cent of global CO₂ emissions comes from cement alone?
config.why: About 7–8%, with steel similar — which is why timber-where-steel-will-do, reclaimed structure and cement substitutes are the embodied-carbon levers.
config.context: A new, efficient building can emit more carbon on construction day than it saves annually for a decade — the greenest building is the one already standing.

activities.anchor: because the organs were value-engineered out
activities.caption: true or false — the building's organs
activities.name: wbServicesJudge

statements.s: Office ventilation is specified in litres per second per person — roughly 8–10 l/s.
statements.why: The CO₂ arithmetic from the shelter section, made contractual.

statements.s: Lighting levels are measured in lux — roughly 300–500 for offices.
statements.why: Higher for detailed work; the number lives in the services schedule.

statements.s: In modern buildings the services cost approaches or exceeds the structure's.
statements.why: Hospitals are machines with rooms attached — in a literal budgetary sense.

statements.s: Services coordination is an electrical problem, not a spatial one.
statements.why: It is spatial: every duct, pipe and cable needs a continuous path without colliding with structure or swallowing floor-to-floor height.
